job.description:
Title: QC Data Reviewer

Pay: $32.00-$40.00/hr

Location: Costa Mesa, CA

Schedule: Standard Office Hrs (On-site)

Duration: Temp-To-Perm, Initial 3-Month Contract




The QC Data Reviewer independently reviews pharmaceutical quality control (QC) laboratory data, analytical results, and supporting documentation to verify accuracy, completeness, traceability, and data integrity. The role covers raw material, in-process, finished product, stability, and other applicable testing. Reviews follow current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), applicable regulatory requirements, approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Good Documentation Practices (GDP), and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.




The QC Data Reviewer works with QC analysts, laboratory supervisors, Quality Assurance (QA), and other departments to resolve discrepancies and support the timely release of laboratory data for quality decisions.



Key Responsibilities

QC Data and Documentation Review

  • Independently review raw data, analytical results, worksheets, laboratory notebooks, and supporting records for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and compliance.
  • Verify that testing follows approved analytical methods, specifications, protocols, and SOPs.
  • Check calculations, dilution factors, standard and sample weights, preparation records, units of measurement, significant figures, and reported results.
  • Verify results against approved acceptance criteria and confirm that atypical or failing results are identified and addressed.
  • Confirm that analyst signatures, dates, instrument references, sample identifiers, and supporting attachments are complete and traceable.
  • Document reviews according to approved procedures and confirm that review comments are resolved before final disposition.

Instrument and Electronic Data Review

  • Review data generated by HPLC, UPLC, GC, UV-Vis, dissolution, and other applicable analytical systems.
  • Evaluate chromatograms, integration parameters, system suitability results, sequence tables, injections, standards, blanks, controls, and sample results as applicable to the method.
  • Review electronic laboratory records, audit trails, metadata, and associated raw data according to approved procedures and risk-based data integrity requirements.
  • Verify that electronic data meet ALCOA+ principles. Identify unexplained data exclusions, undocumented reinjections or reprocessing, unauthorized changes, and missing records.
  • Confirm that applicable instrument qualification, calibration, maintenance, and system suitability requirements have been met.
  • Verify that electronic records and signatures meet applicable requirements, including 21 CFR Part 11 where applicable.

GMP and Regulatory Compliance

  • Verify that laboratory records and data reviews comply with applicable cGMP requirements, approved procedures, specifications, analytical methods, and internal quality standards.
  • Apply GDP to identify incomplete entries, undocumented corrections, missing signatures, inconsistent dates, and inadequate justifications.
  • Follow applicable requirements under 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, relevant FDA guidance, and other applicable regulatory standards.
  • Follow defined reviewer responsibilities and quality system controls, and support data integrity procedures for paper-based and computerized laboratory systems.
  • Maintain inspection-ready records and provide documentation for internal audits, customer audits, and regulatory inspections.

Deviations, OOS/OOT Results, and Investigations

  • Identify and promptly escalate out-of-specification (OOS), out-of-trend (OOT), atypical, or otherwise questionable results.
  • Review documentation for deviations, laboratory events, invalidated results, and investigations.
  • Verify that invalidation, repeat testing, reinjection, reprocessing, and retesting follow approved procedures and have a documented scientific rationale.
  • Document discrepancies and review findings clearly, objectively, and with appropriate traceability.
  • Collaborate with QC analysts, supervisors, and QA to resolve review comments and support timely investigation closure.
  • Escalate suspected data integrity issues through established quality systems and preserve the records in question.

Quality Systems and Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain accurate records of completed reviews, discrepancies, corrections, and approvals.
  • Meet established turnaround times while maintaining review quality and independence.
  • Support document control, change control, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), and other assigned quality system activities.
  • Participate in SOP revisions, process improvements, data review standardization, and compliance initiatives.
  • Assist with documentation and responses for audits, inspections, and internal compliance assessments.
  • Maintain current knowledge of applicable GMP requirements, data integrity expectations, and laboratory procedures.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biology, or a related discipline.
  • Typically 2–5 years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical QC, GMP laboratory operations, QC data review, or a closely related quality function.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of cGMP requirements, GDP, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
  • Practical experience reviewing analytical laboratory records, raw data, calculations, and test results.
  • Ability to identify documentation discrepancies, analytical inconsistencies, and potential compliance concerns.
  • Strong attention to detail, analytical reasoning, written communication, and organizational skills.

Preferred

  • Prior experience in an independent QC data review or laboratory quality review role.
  • Experience with chromatography data systems such as Empower or comparable software.
  • Familiarity with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), electronic laboratory notebooks, other laboratory information systems, and electronic document management systems.
  • Experience reviewing HPLC, UPLC, GC, dissolution, UV-Vis, or other pharmaceutical analytical testing data.
  • Familiarity with OOS/OOT investigations, deviations, CAPA, audit trails, and computerized system controls.
  • Experience supporting FDA, EMA, or other applicable regulatory inspections.

Technical Knowledge and Competencies

  • Knowledge of pharmaceutical analytical testing principles, laboratory workflows, analytical method requirements, system suitability, specifications, and acceptance criteria.
  • Proficiency in reviewing calculations, chromatographic results, instrument-generated records, and supporting documentation.
  • Knowledge of risk-based data integrity review and familiarity with applicable requirements under 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 and, where applicable, Part 11.
  • Ability to evaluate records objectively and distinguish minor documentation deficiencies from significant quality or data integrity concerns.
  • Ability to document review comments clearly, explain findings, manage competing priorities, and meet deadlines while collaborating across QC and QA teams.
  • Professional judgment, independence, confidentiality, and a commitment to product quality and patient safety.
